title: High Temp Lockout
fullDescription: Blodgett deck and convection ovens lock out at E1 when the cavity exceeds safe limits. Causes include stuck contactors, failed thermocouple, or runaway burner control.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power and gas before service.

fixSteps.title: Inspect contactor / gas valve
fixSteps.instruction: Check for welded contacts (electric) or open gas valve (gas).

whenToCallPro: Gas valves and high-voltage contactors should be handled by service techs.

faq.a: Yes, until E1 is diagnosed; runaway heating is a fire hazard.

title: Open Thermocouple
fullDescription: E2 indicates the cavity thermocouple is open or out of range. Without temperature feedback, the controller will not allow heating.
whenToCallPro: If new thermocouple still fails, board may need service.

faq.a: Use OEM types and gauges to ensure accuracy.

title: Door Switch Fault
shortDescription: Door switch open during cook or stuck closed.
fullDescription: Blodgett convection ovens stop convection fans when the door is open. E3 fires when the door switch readings are inconsistent.

fixSteps.title: Check alignment
fixSteps.instruction: Adjust door so plunger fully depresses switch.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement door switch with correct ratings.

whenToCallPro: Hinge alignment may need a service tech for older units.

faq.q: Why are fans tied to door?
faq.a: Safety; prevents fan from drawing flames or fingers when door opens.

title: Convection Fan Fault
shortDescription: Fan stalled or rotation feedback missing.
fullDescription: E4 indicates the convection blower is not running. Without it, hot spots form and the cavity overheats. Causes include failed motor, capacitor, or belt.

fixSteps.title: Inspect belt
fixSteps.instruction: Check belt tension and condition; replace if worn.

whenToCallPro: Motor replacement on convection ovens benefits from a tech.

faq.a: Refer to model service manual; about 1/2 inch deflection at midspan.

title: Ignition Failure (Gas)
shortDescription: Burner did not light within trial-for-ignition.
fullDescription: On gas Blodgett ovens, E5 fires after the ignition module fails to confirm flame. Causes include closed gas, dirty pilot/electrode, weak ignitor, or air in lines.

fixSteps.title: Verify gas supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm shutoffs open, supply pressure correct.

fixSteps.title: Clean ignitor/flame sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Use fine emery to clean rod; check spark gap.

whenToCallPro: Gas system work should be done by qualified service.

faq.a: Shut off supply, ventilate, do not operate switches, call a gas technician.

title: Heating Element Open (Electric)
shortDescription: One or more heating elements open circuit.
fullDescription: E6 detects an open element on electric Blodgett ovens. Without full bank of elements the cavity cannot reach setpoint quickly enough.

fixSteps.title: Test elements
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, measure resistance per element; replace any open.

whenToCallPro: Element replacement involves disassembly and high voltage; consider service.

faq.a: Recommended on older ovens to extend service interval.

title: Cooling Fan Fault
fullDescription: Blodgett ovens use a small fan to cool the controls. E7 indicates the fan stalled. Risk of control failure if ignored.

fixSteps.title: Replace cooling fan
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; replace fan with OEM part.

whenToCallPro: Operator-friendly with basic skill; tech if disassembly is unfamiliar.

faq.a: On the rear or side of the control housing.

title: Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: Supply voltage out of nameplate range.
fullDescription: E8 indicates the controller has detected mains voltage too high or low. Operating outside spec damages motors and electronics.

fixSteps.title: Verify supply
fixSteps.instruction: Measure voltage at terminal block under load.

whenToCallPro: Building electrical work needs licensed electrician.

faq.a: If supply is consistently out of range, fix the wiring or upgrade circuit.

title: Steam Generator Fault
shortDescription: Steam injection system fault on combi/steam-injected models.
fullDescription: On steam-capable Blodgett ovens, E9 indicates the steam generator did not reach setpoint or has scaled boilers/clogged solenoid.

fixSteps.title: Descale
fixSteps.instruction: Run Blodgett descaling routine with approved solution.

whenToCallPro: Heater replacement and pressurized steam systems require service.

faq.a: No, use approved descaler to avoid damage.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Loss of communication between display and main board.
fullDescription: E10 indicates a broken communication link between user interface and main board. Loose harness, moisture, or board failure are possibilities.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat ribbon and harnesses.

title: Steam Probe Open
shortDescription: Steam generator level probe open circuit.
fullDescription: Combi steam-generator water level long probe is open.
whenToCallPro: Sealed-system, gas, and high-voltage diagnosis on this unit requires a licensed commercial tech. Commercial appliance work in foodservice settings requires a licensed/EPA-certified technician for refrigerant, gas, or high-voltage components.
